title: Word 19 — On Sin
attribution_note: Word 19 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: O beloved creature of God! Where is your fair beauty, the image and likeness of God? Where is your holiness, your purity, your righteousness? *“And man, being in honor, did not understand this; he became like the senseless beasts and was made like unto them.”* Terribly does the holy apostle describe and set before our inward eyes the man who has not been renewed by God's grace: *“There is none righteous, no, not one; there is none that understandeth; there is none that seeketh after God.* *They have all gone out of the way; they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.* *Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips; whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways; and the way of peace have they not known; there is no fear of God before their eyes”* [Romans 3:10–18].

sections.heading: Why Sin Is So Great an Evil

pairs.en: 2) No one can take sin away from man except the Son of God. For this very purpose — to take away sin — He came into the world, suffered, and died, that He might destroy sin. *“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil”* [1 John 3:8]. *“Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world”* [John 1:29]. Glory to His love for mankind!

5) For sin come temporal punishments: famine, fire, war, plague, sickness, earthquake, and the rest. *“Death, and bloodshed, and strife, and sword, calamities, famine, and tribulation, and the scourge — all these things were created for the wicked,”* says Sirach [Sirach 40:9–10]. “Sins are the cause of every evil,” says St. John Chrysostom. See, then, how great an evil sin is — an evil worse than every other evil. O, truly it is better to go naked than to sin; better to sit in captivity and in prison than to sin. Better to suffer wounds and every sickness than to sin. Better never to see the light and to sit in darkness than to sin. Better to endure mockery, scorn, reproach, slander, blows, and wounds than to sin; better, in short, to endure whatever evil there may be in this world than to sin! For each of these evils torments only the body, and only for a time, since death puts an end to all suffering — there every calamity comes to a close. But sin torments both body and soul, and will torment without end forever. For sin is the cause of every calamity that befalls in this world, as was said above. Had there been no sin, there would have been no calamity. Sin began in the world, and every calamity followed after it. Sin is sweet to men, but its fruits are bitter. A bitter seed bears bitter fruit as well.

sections.heading: Know Sin, That You May Flee It

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! Let us come to know sin, that we may turn away from it, for every man turns away from an evil he has come to know. People know that poison is harmful, and they avoid it. They know that the serpent kills with its sting, and they guard against it. They know that robbers plunder and kill, and they avoid them. Let us too, beloved, come to know sin and the evil that flows from it, and we will surely turn away from it. For sin is more harmful than any poison, sin is more venomous than any serpent, sin strips us more bare than any robber, deprives us of temporal and eternal blessings, and kills both body and soul. Such are the fruits of sin's bitter seed.

sections.heading: The Many Faces of Sin, Part One

pairs.en: Sin is shameful talk, foul language, foolish speech, blasphemy, and every corrupt word.

sections.heading: The Many Faces of Sin, Part Two

pairs.en: Sin is adultery, fornication, and every uncleanness.

sections.heading: Sin Is Worse Than the Demons

pairs.en: O Christ, the true Light, who gavest light to the blind, enlighten also the eyes of our hearts, that we may know sin and turn away from sin! The beginning of salvation is to know one's own wretchedness. Amen.
